# Background Verification for Schools, Colleges, and EdTech Companies in India: Protecting Students \[2026\]


September 22, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/background-verification-for-schools-colleges-and-edtech-companies-in-india-protecting-students-2026/#respond)


Background verification in the education sector in India is fundamentally a child and student safety measure because teachers, tutors, administrative staff, and support workers in schools, colleges, coaching centres, and edtech companies have direct, often unsupervised access to minors and young adults, making identity verification through PAN, Voter ID, and employment history checks through UAN an essential safeguard that digital platforms like Compose1 Verify can complete in under 30 minutes per candidate.


Education is the second largest employer in India after agriculture. The sector includes over 15 lakh schools (government and private), 50,000 colleges and universities, lakhs of coaching centres and tuition providers, and a rapidly growing edtech industry with companies hiring thousands of teachers and content creators. Collectively, these institutions employ crores of teachers, professors, tutors, administrative staff, and support workers.


Every one of these employees interacts with students. In schools, that means minors. In colleges, that means young adults away from home for the first time. In coaching centres, that means students under academic pressure. In edtech, that means learners who trust the platform’s quality standards.


The trust that parents and students place in educational institutions is built on the assumption that the institution has vetted its staff. That the biology teacher is actually qualified to teach biology. That the school bus driver has a valid licence. That the hostel warden’s identity has been confirmed. That the online tutor is who they claim to be.


In reality, verification in the education sector is patchy at best. Government schools rely on the selection process (exams and interviews) but rarely verify documents against databases. Private schools check certificates visually but do not query government databases. Coaching centres hire tutors based on subject knowledge tests without verifying identity at all. EdTech companies assess teaching ability through demo sessions but skip background checks.


This guide explains why education sector verification is uniquely important, what checks are needed for different roles, how institutions of all sizes can verify staff affordably, and how digital verification addresses the specific challenges of education hiring.


## Why Education Verification Is a Safety Priority


### Direct Access to Minors


In schools (K-12), every employee has access to children. Teachers spend 6 to 8 hours daily with students. Support staff (peons, sweepers, security guards) move freely through school premises where children are present. School bus drivers transport children without parental supervision. Hostel wardens supervise children 24/7 during the school year.


An unverified individual with a fake identity in any of these roles has unsupervised access to minors with no accountability trail. If an incident occurs, the school cannot even identify who the individual actually is because the documents on file are fraudulent.


### POCSO Act 2012 Implications


The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act creates specific obligations for institutions that work with children. While POCSO does not explicitly mandate background verification, it establishes strict liability for institutions that fail to protect children in their care. A school that deploys an unverified employee who subsequently harms a child faces both POCSO liability and civil liability for negligent hiring.


Courts have increasingly held educational institutions responsible for ensuring the safety of students. The duty of care includes, at minimum, confirming that staff members are who they claim to be.


### Credential Fraud in Teaching


Teaching credential fraud in India takes several forms. Individuals with fake B.Ed or M.Ed degrees teaching in schools without proper qualifications. Tutors claiming expertise in subjects they are not qualified to teach. “Experienced” teachers whose claimed 10 years of experience is actually 2 years at one school. Coaches and counsellors with fabricated psychology or counselling credentials.


The consequences of credential fraud in education extend beyond the immediate institution. An unqualified science teacher can teach incorrect concepts to hundreds of students over years. An unqualified counsellor can provide harmful advice to vulnerable students. An unqualified physical education teacher can fail to maintain safety standards during sports activities.


### Transport Safety


School transportation is one of the highest-risk activities in education. School buses and vans transport children daily, often in heavy traffic and on routes involving multiple stops. Every year, India reports school bus accidents caused by driver negligence, unfit vehicles, and in some cases, unlicensed drivers.


DL verification for school bus and van drivers is not a luxury. It is a direct child safety requirement. A driver with a suspended licence transporting 40 children is an unacceptable risk that a 2-minute DL check eliminates.


## The Education Sector Verification Framework


### Category 1: Teaching Staff (Schools)


Teachers are the core of any educational institution. They have the most extensive access to students and the greatest influence on student outcomes.


**Required checks:**


**PAN Verification:** Confirms the teacher’s identity against the Income Tax Department database. Ensures TDS compliance for salary payments. Catches fake PANs and deactivated PANs.


**Voter ID Verification:** Cross-confirms identity through the Election Commission database. The cross-record analysis between PAN and Voter ID catches identity fraud. A teacher using someone else’s identity and qualifications is detected when the name or date of birth does not match across documents.


**UAN Employment History:** Confirms teaching experience claimed during hiring. A teacher hired as “10 years experienced” at Rs 50,000 per month should have that employment history reflected in EPFO records. UAN verification catches experience inflation that affects both the salary offered and the responsibility assigned.


**How to do it:** Enter PAN, Voter ID, and UAN on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Total time: 15 to 30 minutes. Cost: Rs 300 to Rs 800 per teacher.


**Additionally required:** Teaching degree and qualification verification with the issuing university. This is separate from the identity checks on Compose1 Verify and must be done directly with the institution or through a specialized education verification provider.


### Category 2: Teaching Staff (Colleges and Universities)


College and university faculty members have access to young adults, research data, examination processes, and institutional reputation.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID + UAN through Compose1 Verify. Same rationale as school teachers, with the additional consideration that university faculty often hold multiple positions (visiting faculty at multiple institutions) and UAN helps confirm the claimed employment pattern.


### Category 3: School Transport Staff


Bus drivers, van drivers, and transport attendants are responsible for children during transit. This is one of the highest-risk roles in the education sector.


**Required checks:**


**PAN + Voter ID:** Identity confirmation. A driver operating under a fake identity is unaccountable and untraceable if an incident occurs.


**DL Verification:** Non-negotiable. Every driver must have a valid DL verified against VAHAN/SARATHI through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Confirm the licence is valid, not expired, not suspended, and authorized for the vehicle class (buses require specific authorization beyond LMV).


**How to do it:** PAN + Voter ID + DL through Compose1 Verify. Total time: 10 to 15 minutes. Cost: Rs 200 to Rs 600 per driver.


**Re-verification frequency:** Quarterly. DL status can change between checks (suspension for traffic violations, expiry). A quarterly DL check costs Rs 50 to Rs 200 and takes 2 minutes. This is the minimum standard for anyone driving children.


### Category 4: Administrative Staff


Office administrators, accounts staff, admissions officers, and front office personnel handle student records, fee payments, examination data, and parent communications.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. Administrative staff who handle financial transactions (fee collection, vendor payments) need verified identities for accountability. Staff with access to student records need verified identities under DPDP Act data handling requirements.


### Category 5: Support Staff


Housekeeping, security guards, peons, lab attendants, library staff, and maintenance workers have physical access to the institution and proximity to students.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID. These roles involve unsupervised access to areas where students are present. A security guard’s identity must be confirmed because they are entrusted with campus security. A lab attendant’s identity must be confirmed because they handle chemicals and equipment in the presence of students. A hostel warden’s identity must be confirmed because they supervise students 24/7.


### Category 6: Coaching Centre and Tuition Staff


Coaching centres operate with less regulatory oversight than schools. Many hire tutors based on subject knowledge without formal verification. This creates significant risk because coaching centre tutors often have one-on-one or small-group sessions with students, sometimes at the student’s home.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID for every tutor. UAN for tutors hired based on claimed teaching experience. These checks take 10 to 20 minutes and cost Rs 100 to Rs 800 per tutor.


### Category 7: EdTech Employees


EdTech companies hire teachers for online classes, content creators for course material, mentors for student guidance, and operations staff who handle student data. Many of these employees work remotely and never physically meet students.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID for all employees. UAN for experienced hires. The remote nature of edtech work makes digital verification through Compose1 Verify a natural fit. The employee is remote, the verification is digital, and the results are government-database-confirmed.


## Education-Specific Fraud Patterns


### Pattern 1: The Teacher with Fake Qualifications


A private school in Rajasthan hires a “B.Ed qualified” science teacher based on a certificate that looks genuine. The teacher’s classroom performance is adequate for two years. When the school applies for CBSE affiliation upgrade, the board’s inspection reveals that the B.Ed certificate is from a university that does not exist. The school loses its affiliation application, the teacher is terminated, and the school faces reputational damage.


While qualification verification requires contact with the issuing university, identity verification through PAN + Voter ID at the time of hiring would have at least confirmed whether the person was who they claimed to be. Cross-record analysis catches identity fraud, which often accompanies credential fraud (using someone else’s identity along with fabricated qualifications).


### Pattern 2: The School Bus Driver with a Suspended DL


A school in Madhya Pradesh employs a bus driver through a transport contractor. The contractor assures the school that “all our drivers have valid licences.” The driver has a DL, but it was suspended 4 months ago for a drunk driving incident. Two months later, the driver is involved in an accident that injures 3 children. Insurance denies the claim due to the suspended DL. The school faces Rs 8 lakh in medical expenses, criminal prosecution under POCSO-adjacent provisions (negligent endangerment of children), and parent protests.


A DL verification costing Rs 100 would have caught the suspension before the driver was assigned to the school bus.


### Pattern 3: The Tutor with a Hidden Identity


A coaching centre in Delhi hires a home tutor for mathematics. The tutor provides a PAN and address proof. Over 6 months, three parents report that the tutor made their daughters uncomfortable with inappropriate comments during private sessions. When the coaching centre tries to take action, they discover the PAN belongs to a different person. The tutor’s real identity is unknown. The coaching centre cannot cooperate with police because the identity documents on file are fraudulent.


PAN + Voter ID verification through Compose1 Verify would have caught the identity mismatch before the first student session.


### Pattern 4: The Experienced Professor Who Was Not


A private university hires an “Associate Professor” at Rs 1.2 lakh per month based on a resume claiming 12 years at three established universities. The professor’s research output is minimal and teaching feedback is poor. A belated UAN check reveals EPFO records showing only 3 years of formal employment at one university (as an assistant lecturer, not associate professor). The remaining 9 years were fabricated.


The university overpaid by approximately Rs 50,000 per month (the difference between the associate professor and assistant lecturer salary bands) for over a year: Rs 6 lakh in excess salary, plus the opportunity cost of the role being filled by an underqualified individual.


## Implementation by Institution Type


### Government Schools


Government school teacher recruitment goes through centralized selection processes (TET, state exams). However, contractual teachers, guest teachers, and support staff are often hired locally with minimal verification.


**Process:** Run PAN + Voter ID verification for all contractual and guest teachers through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) before classroom assignment. Run DL verification for all school transport drivers. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400 per person.


### Private Schools (Budget and Mid-Range)


Private schools hire teachers directly, often through advertisements and walk-in interviews. Verification is typically limited to visual certificate inspection.


**Process:** Add digital verification to the hiring process. After interview selection, collect PAN and Voter ID numbers. Run verification through Compose1 Verify. Add UAN for experienced hires. Add DL for transport staff. Total cost: Rs 200 to Rs 800 per hire.


For a school with 50 staff, annual verification cost (including re-verification): Rs 15,000 to Rs 40,000.


### Elite Private Schools and International Schools


These schools have higher budgets and parental expectations. Comprehensive verification aligns with the premium positioning.


**Process:** PAN + Voter ID + UAN for all staff. DL for transport. Extended checks (criminal records, education verification) for all teaching staff through a supplementary provider. Digital identity verification through Compose1 Verify provides the immediate identity layer. Extended checks provide the comprehensive layer.


### Coaching Centres and Tuition Providers


Coaching centres range from large chains to single-person operations. Even the smallest provider should verify tutor identity.


**Process:** At minimum, PAN + Voter ID for every tutor before the first student session. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400 per tutor. For a coaching centre with 10 tutors, annual cost: Rs 1,000 to Rs 4,000. This is less than one student’s monthly fee.


### EdTech Companies


EdTech companies hire at scale, often remotely, and need a verification process that works entirely digitally.


**Process:** PAN + Voter ID for all employees (teaching and non-teaching). UAN for experienced hires. Compose1 Verify’s digital-first model aligns perfectly with edtech’s remote hiring workflow. One HR coordinator can verify 20 to 30 candidates per day.


For an edtech company hiring 200 teachers per year: Rs 40,000 to Rs 160,000 annually.


## Building a School Verification Policy


### Policy Statement


“\[School Name\] is committed to student safety and verifies the identity and credentials of all staff before they are permitted to interact with students. This includes teaching staff, administrative staff, support staff, transport staff, and any contractor-deployed personnel on school premises.”


### Verification Requirements


All staff: PAN + Voter ID verification through Compose1 Verify before first day. Transport staff: DL verification before first drive. Quarterly re-verification. Experienced hires: UAN verification for roles where salary is based on experience. Teaching staff: Qualification verification with issuing university (separate from Compose1 Verify).


### Timing


No staff member shall begin duties until identity verification is complete. Transport staff shall not operate any vehicle until DL verification is confirmed. For contract and outsourced staff, verification must be completed before the individual enters school premises.


### Documentation


PDF verification reports from Compose1 Verify stored in each staff member’s file. Verification register maintained in the school office. Reports available for CBSE/ICSE/state board inspections, parent queries, and regulatory audits.


### Annual Re-Verification


Annual PAN re-verification for all staff. Quarterly DL re-verification for transport staff. Re-verification when staff members change roles or take on additional responsibilities involving students.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is background verification mandatory for school teachers in India?


No single law mandates background verification for all school teachers. However, CBSE and some state boards require schools to maintain verified staff records. The Right to Education Act requires qualified teachers (implying qualification verification). POCSO creates liability for institutions that fail to protect children, making staff verification a practical necessity. Schools that skip verification face legal exposure, reputational risk, and potential loss of affiliation.


### How much does it cost to verify school staff?


PAN + Voter ID verification costs Rs 100 to Rs 400 per person through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Adding UAN costs Rs 300 to Rs 800 total. Adding DL costs Rs 200 to Rs 600 total. For a school with 50 staff, comprehensive digital verification costs Rs 10,000 to Rs 40,000 per year. Compare this to the cost of one incident involving an unverified staff member.


### Should schools verify bus drivers themselves or trust the transport contractor?


Verify them yourself. The school has a duty of care for children during transport. The transport contractor’s incentive is to deploy drivers quickly, not to verify them thoroughly. Run DL verification through Compose1 Verify for every driver before their first trip. Re-verify quarterly. Cost: Rs 50 to Rs 200 per driver per quarter. This is the minimum standard for anyone driving children.


### How do coaching centres verify part-time tutors?


Collect PAN and Voter ID numbers from every tutor before their first student session. Run verification through Compose1 Verify. Total time: 10 minutes per tutor. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400. This applies to full-time faculty, part-time tutors, home tutors, and online tutors. The student’s safety is the same regardless of the tutor’s employment type.


### Can edtech companies use digital verification for remote teachers?


Yes, and they should. Digital verification through Compose1 Verify is designed for remote workflows. The teacher shares their document numbers online, the edtech company runs verification digitally, and results are confirmed against government databases without any physical meeting. This is the ideal verification method for edtech’s remote hiring model.


### How do I verify a teacher’s educational qualifications?


Educational qualification verification (B.Ed, M.Ed, subject degrees) requires contacting the issuing university or using a specialized education verification provider. This is separate from the identity and employment verification that Compose1 Verify handles (PAN, Voter ID, UAN, DL). Both types of verification are important: Compose1 Verify confirms who the person is, education verification confirms what they studied.


### What records should schools maintain for staff verification?


For each staff member: PAN verification report (PDF), Voter ID verification report (PDF), DL verification report (for transport staff), UAN verification report (for experienced hires), qualification verification records, consent form, and verification date. Maintain for the duration of employment plus two years. These records satisfy board inspection requirements and demonstrate due diligence in case of any incidents.


### Should schools verify contract housekeeping and security staff?


Yes. Contract housekeeping and security staff have physical access to school premises where children are present. A security guard controls who enters the campus. Housekeeping staff access classrooms, washrooms, and common areas. Verify every contract worker’s identity (PAN + Voter ID) through Compose1 Verify before they begin work on school premises. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400 per worker.


## Every Adult on Your Campus Deserves a Verified Identity


Parents trust schools with their children. That trust carries an obligation: every adult who interacts with those children should be verified as who they claim to be. Not just the teachers. Not just the senior staff. Every security guard, every bus driver, every lab attendant, every contract worker who enters the school gates.


Digital verification makes this possible without breaking the school’s budget or slowing down hiring. Fifteen minutes per person. Under Rs 500 per check. Government-database-confirmed identity. That is the baseline every educational institution in India should meet.
